key_insight: Auxiliary-space multigrid preconditioners let conforming finite element solvers use coarse meshes built entirely by agglomeration, without requiring conforming coarse meshes.
engineering_relevance: This approach can simplify scalable finite element solver construction on complex engineering geometries by relaxing coarse-mesh constraints.
method: Precondition fine-mesh conforming Lagrange elements with coarse polytopal DG or hybrid high-order discretisations.
Build subsequent multigrid levels by further agglomeration.
Transfer coarse solutions through element-wise interpolation and nodal averaging, with local potential reconstruction for hybrid high-order elements.
evidence_signal: Experiments in 2D and 3D on structured and unstructured meshes with automatically clustered agglomerates support robustness; proven condition-number bounds are O((H/h)^3), improving to O((H/h)^2) for DG with appropriately scaled penalty.
watch_item: Condition-number bounds worsen with the coarsening ratio H/h, so aggressive agglomeration requires care.
paper_title: Geometric Multigrid Preconditioners for conforming Finite Element Methods on Arbitrarily Agglomerated Meshes
